summary: Patrick Pranke works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, where he studied under Luis O. Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman (attested 2004).

Patrick R. Uhlmann specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he was a PhD candidate attested in 2012, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Patrick de Silva Kularatne (1893–1976) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at University College London and the University of London (~1913–1917) and served as principal of Ananda College (~1918–1943).

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1828–1843) and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Paul B. Courtright is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998; Professor Emeritus attested 2026).

Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Yeshe Thapkay, Losang Yarphel, and Geshe Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Bernard (1929–2015) was a historian and archaeologist of Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and Sorbonne, he directed the DAFA (1965–1980) and held posts at the CNRS and EPHE (1981).

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a philosopher and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Hermann Grassmann and attended Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (PhD ~1876), later working at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

Paul Copp specializes in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD attested 2005 under Stephen F. Teiser), he has held posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe works in sinology and religious studies. He completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and held a professorship at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Nizam College, Presidency University, and Yale (doctorate ~1931), he taught at United Theological College (1932–1949) and directed CISRS from 1956.

Paul David Numrich works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan in 1992 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus (attested 2006).

Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a Buddhist studies figure. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955), and served on the board of the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg.

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. His career included posts at EFEO (1920–1924), INALCO, EPHE, and the Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Christian Lassen and at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin. He taught at RWTH Aachen (~1873–1879), Berlin (1881–1887), and Kiel University from 1889.
Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he led Asian studies there (~1976–2023) and served as head of the Pali Text Society.
Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held a long-term academic post at the University of California, San Francisco (~1960–2004).

Paul F. Knitter (1939–) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1958–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1969–1972), and served at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2017).

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège (doctorate ~1875). He was a professor at Liège (~1879–1883) and at Ghent University from 1883, serving as its rector in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin, also studying under Paul Dundas, and held a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).
